title: mhdturbFoam-hardened: a corrected redistribution of the FOSSEE mhdturbFoam turbulent MHD solver for OpenFOAM 6
description:
A hardened redistribution of the FOSSEE mhdturbFoam solver for incompressible turbulent magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) flows in OpenFOAM 6, using the full magnetic-induction formulation inherited from OpenFOAM's mhdFoam. The Lorentz force is evaluated in Maxwell-stress form from the total field and the divergence constraint on B is enforced through a magnetic flux pressure pB (B-PISO loop).

This is a derived work, not an original formulation. The physical formulation and numerical structure belong to OpenFOAM's mhdFoam, and the turbulent skeleton to the FOSSEE mhdturbFoam case-study project (R. Radhakrishnan, 2019). The contribution of this package is the correction of three numerical defects of the upstream derivative, plus the verification suite and packaging.

Corrections: (1) the outer PISO corrector loop is restored, so that rAU, HbyA and phiHbyA are recomputed at every corrector and the pFinal solver dictionary is actually reached; (2) the singular pB Poisson problem of closed or fully periodic domains is given a reference cell/value, read optionally from the BPISO dictionary; (3) fvOptions are coupled into the momentum equation (fvOptions(U) and fvOptions.constrain(UEqn)), which is required by fv::meanVelocityForce to drive a periodic channel.

The package contains the solver source and build files, and three verification cases built on the geometry and boundary-condition layout of the standard OpenFOAM 6 mhdFoam Hartmann tutorial (100x40x1 mesh): a transverse-field channel, a spanwise-field channel with B = (0 0 -B), and a streamwise-periodic channel driven by meanVelocityForce that exercises all three corrections. All cases reach completion with maximum continuity errors below 1e-7, maximum magnetic flux divergence errors below 1e-9, and a final pressure residual of about 1e-6 (the pFinal tolerance). A verification script reproduces the reported metrics.
